chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muyassir ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man bought a skin-container of oil and found sediment in it, so he said:
“If he was among those who know that such a thing occurs in oil, he should not return it to him. But if he did not know that such a thing occurs in oil, he may return it to him.”

key_terms.دُرْدِيًّا: sediment, dregs, or residue found at the bottom of oil
key_terms.رَدَّهُ: he returned it or has the right to return it in this context
key_terms.زَيْتٍ: oil being discussed as the sold commodity
key_terms.زِقَّ: a skin-container or vessel used for storing liquids
key_terms.يَرُدَّهُ: returns it, meaning sends back the purchased item
key_terms.يَعْلَمُ: knows or is aware of the customary nature of the matter

ai.seo_question: Can a buyer return oil if sediment is found in it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about returning a purchased good after discovering a common defect or residue. If the buyer knew that such sediment is normally present in oil, he has no right of return; if he did not know, he may return it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3977 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrates from Muyassir ibn Abdul Aziz, who said:
I asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), about a man who bought a container of oil and found sediment (dregs) in it.

Imam (as) said: "If the buyer was aware that such sediment is commonly found in oil, he cannot return it. However, if he was unaware that such sediment is usually present, he has the right to return it."
